answer: Each agent must build a persistent reputation by completing randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked by unrelated agents before rewards are released. A new identity has no history, so creating many accounts does not inherit trusted status; each must earn its own record. Random assignments act as a zephyr exposing copied claims, while even a velvet-smooth cluster must pay to operate accounts over time and risk losing stakes if audits reveal collusion. That cost makes the trust signal harder to forge.
